title: Russian Missile Strikes Hit Zaporizhstal and ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih Steel Plants, Killing Two
detail: Russian forces struck two of Ukraine's largest steel plants overnight into September 12. Four ballistic missiles hit the Zaporizhstal plant in Zaporizhzhia, operator Metinvest said, injuring four employees and causing what the company described as critical damage — the third ballistic missile strike on the plant in a month, after attacks on August 11 and August 27, and the plant had not resumed production from the prior strikes. Separately, a missile — assessed by Ukraine's Air Force as a likely Iskander-K — hit the ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih plant in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, killing two subcontractor employees and wounding four.

title: Russian Missile and Drone Assault Sets 25-Story Odesa High-Rise Ablaze
detail: Russia launched a mass missile-and-drone assault on the Odesa region overnight into September 12, involving roughly 129 drones plus cruise and ballistic missiles targeting residential buildings, energy infrastructure and the port complex. A fire engulfed multiple upper floors of the 25-story Kadorr apartment tower; strikes also damaged gas lines, private homes and a rehabilitation facility. Casualty tolls varied by outlet: Kyiv Independent reported at least 12 injured, while Ukrainian officials cited elsewhere put the toll at 2 killed and up to 26 injured. The strike continued a months-long Russian campaign against Greater Odesa's ports (Odesa, Chornomorsk, Pivdennyi).

title: Ukraine's Navy Wins History's First Drone-vs-Drone Naval Battle in the Black Sea
detail: Ukraine's Navy, operating jointly with military intelligence (HUR), said its Sargan 3000 uncrewed surface vessel destroyed a Russian unmanned MBeK-type boat in the Black Sea on September 12 — the first recorded battle in history between two uncrewed naval vessels. The Sargan 3000, armed with a 12.7mm Protector remote weapons station, opened fire from roughly one kilometer away; the Russian drone boat attempted to flee but was immobilized and destroyed. The engagement underscores the rapid expansion of unmanned warfare to the maritime domain in the Black Sea theater.
